title: Wait only for the 'fmt, clippy, tests' check run before landing push
summary: The pre-push wait in gh.rs (wait_for_early_run) ends at any failed workflow run on the early candidate. Because the candidate's history and PR-head jobs always fail, it never waits for the cached job. Read the candidate's check run named 'fmt, clippy, tests' only: wait until it completes, push at once if it failed, and ignore the other jobs' conclusions. The audience is the maintainer running land, who wants it to stop taking 18 minutes.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus clippy and fmt clean.
Criteria exercise wait versus push-at-once through the fake host.
Fix the wait's selection of runs, not the timeout.
One focused change in gh.rs and the changelog.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Workflow-run data (ci_runs) cannot name a job, so a PrHost method reads the commit's check runs (the check-runs endpoint already used by checks) and picks the one named 'fmt, clippy, tests'; all PrHost implementations (real, test_support fakes, gh.rs test hosts) are updated.
A missing named check run is treated like no runs: push at once; timeout and unreadable replies behave as before.
The 20-second step and the bound are unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new fake-host test in gh.rs: the candidate has a failed history job and 'fmt, clippy, tests' in progress then completed; land polls (sleeps) until 'fmt, clippy, tests' completes and only then replaces the early head. Run cargo test -p athena-core and see it pass.

A new test: 'fmt, clippy, tests' on the candidate is already failed, with the other jobs in any state; land pushes at once with no sleeping and the note says that job failed. Run cargo test -p athena-core.
Existing early-run tests (waits before pushing, pushes at once when completed, pushes anyway on timeout, unreadable or no runs) still pass, and cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check are clean.

wait_for_early_run no longer ends on any failed workflow run; it decides only from the check run named 'fmt, clippy, tests' (a constant), found through the host seam, and its doc comment says so and why (a candidate is not a landing).
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the changed wait.

out_of_scope: Changing the CI workflow or job names
Changing wait_for_checks after the landing push
urgent_reason: Cuts a wasted 18-minute landing wait: the early wait gives up on a failure that always happens, so it redoes work the cache would have saved.
